item.text:
**4B.3 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador (2024)**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning negative. There is some evidence of procedural tolerance for opposition victory and limited legal restraint around criticism, but the year’s stronger record is hostile rhetoric toward critics, intimidation of journalists, surveillance concerns, and coercive policing of protest.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| México | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico | The Reuters Institute says Gálvez obtained a court order for a right of reply to AMLO’s false claims, which is positive evidence that criticism could still force a legal response rather than being fully shut down. | 4B.3 |
| Tribunal Electoral valida elección presidencial: Segob; presidente celebra ejemplar transición en gobierno federal | Presidencia de México | 2024-08-13 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/tribunal-electoral-valida-eleccion-presidencial-segob-presidente-celebra-ejemplar-transicion-en-gobierno-federal/ | After the tribunal validated the election, AMLO’s government publicly celebrated an “ejemplar transición,” which is direct evidence of tolerating an opposition victory and transition of power. | 4B.3, 4B.1 |
| 20.05.24 Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador | Presidencia de México | 2024-05-20 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/20-05-24-version-estenografica-de-la-conferencia-de-prensa-matutina-del-presidente-andres-manuel-lopez-obrador/ | AMLO said conservatives were “adversaries, not enemies” and that repression, authoritarianism, and censorship were unnecessary. That is limited positive evidence for tolerating dissent rhetorically. | 4B.3 |
| México | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says civil society members still freely criticize state policies, but also notes that AMLO’s dismissive and insulting treatment of critics generated tension. This is mixed evidence: criticism remained possible, but the climate was hostile. | 4B.3 |
| Mexico City police arrest 2 journalists at human rights protest | Committee to Protect Journalists | 2024-09-09 | https://cpj.org/2024/09/mexico-city-police-arrest-2-journalists-at-human-rights-protest/ | CPJ reported police beat and arrested journalists covering a human-rights protest, which is direct negative evidence against tolerating protest and monitoring. | 4B.3, 3B.8 |
| Mexico: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says protests are frequent, but police frequently use excessive force and arbitrarily detain protesters; environmental activists and Indigenous groups are especially vulnerable. That is strong negative evidence on protest tolerance. | 4B.3, 3B.8 |
| México | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico | The Reuters Institute says AMLO’s final year featured regular verbal attacks on journalists, human rights advocates, and the media. This is negative evidence on tolerance of criticism and investigative journalism. | 4B.3, 3B.3, 3B.8 |
| México | Reuters via Yahoo News Canada | 2024-02-26 | https://ca.news.yahoo.com/mexicos-president-defends-decision-share-174417727.html | AMLO publicly displayed a New York Times journalist’s phone number and defended the move, a concrete intimidation episode against critical journalism. | 4B.3, 3B.3 |
| Mexico | Amnesty International / CPJ | 2024-03-06 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/mexico-killings-journalists-strengthen-federal-mechanism/ | Amnesty and CPJ reported that journalists under the federal protection mechanism were still being killed, showing the state was not reliably protecting investigative journalism. | 4B.3, 3B.7, 3B.8 |

**Search gap:** I found clear evidence on protests, journalism, and civil-society monitoring, but much less direct evidence on satire specifically. The record is strongest on intimidation of journalists and coercive policing, not on a distinct satire-vs.-tolerance line.
